correction.textOverride: The light from even our nearest stellar neighbour take four years to reach us. When we look at the stars, we is looking back in time. This are an incredible gift. We can see parts of space, parts of our universe, as they was many years ago. The further we can collect light from, the further back in time we could look. If you look at the bright star Betelgeuse, which glow in the Orion constellation, you wind time back more than six hundred years. Its reddish glow start its journey to Earth in the Middle Ages. The stars in Orion’s belt is even further away. Their light, familiar to generations of humans, have travelled at least 1,000 years to reach us. This mean we have a chance of understanding the history of the universe because we can see the more distant parts of it as they were in the past, thousands or millions or billions of years ago.
